info.title: Entity Mapping API
info.description: API Backend for mapping source entity into target entities

parameters.name: with_id
parameters.description: Whether ids are part of the body or not

get.description: Get latest version of a mapping config by id

429.description: Storage stayed throttled, nothing is lost. Repeat the request after `Retry-After` seconds.

get.description: Get specific version of a mapping config by id & version

post.description: Execute entity mapping based on a config

parameters.name: preview_mode
parameters.description: True, if you want to preview the entities which will result

200.description: The target entities which were mapped

post.description: Analyse a stored map-entity action config (engine JSON) line by line: a verdict per line (form, json, broken), issues on the engine line they belong to, suggested rewrites and a sentence each. `valid` is false when an issue is an error; a save gate rejects the config then. Never persists anything. The smallest request is `{ config, source: { journey_id } }`. Send `source` (the trigger's journey or entity schema) instead of `roots.source`, and leave out `target_root` when `config.target_schema` is set: the server loads those descriptions with the caller's authorization. The response is about 1.1 KB per line: from about 5000 lines in one request it exceeds the inline limit (413, see there).

400.description: The request body is malformed: missing fields, a `roots` or `target_root` of the wrong shape, a mapping line without a text `target`, a line or relation target that names `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype`, or a config the validator cannot read (for example nested too deeply). Malformed operations and relations are not a 400: they come back as issues. Caller input never yields a 500.

post.description: Analyse every mapping action (`map-entity`, `cart-checkout`) of an automation, each in its place: against the trigger's source, the entities the earlier actions create and its target schema. The source and every target schema are loaded by id with the caller's authorization. `blocking` lists what a save gate rejects: errors, issues on broken lines and values that are not an option of their attribute. With `previous_actions` (the automation as stored) only issues this change introduced block. Never persists anything. Responses above the inline limit are a 413 (see there).

200.description: The analyses and what blocks a save

400.description: The request body is malformed: no `actions`, duplicate action ids, a `source` of the wrong shape, a mapping line without a text `target` or one naming `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype`, or a config the validator cannot read. Caller input never yields a 500.

post.description: Execute relation mapping between source entity and target entities

200.description: The relations which were for both source entity and main entity

get.description: Get latest version of a mapping config by id V2

put.description: Stores new version of entity mapping config. The targets are not checked on store: check them first with `POST /v1/mappings:validate-flow` (`{ source: { journey_id }, actions: [{ id, type: map-entity, config: <target> }] }`, one action per target) and fix every `blocking` issue.

MappingCheckUnauthorized.description: No `Authorization` header. Sent by the API Gateway authorizer.

MappingCheckForbidden.description: The token is not valid (unsigned, expired, malformed, or sent without the `Bearer ` prefix). Sent by the API Gateway authorizer.

MappingCheckTooLarge.description: The request or the response is too large. Requests above 6 MB are rejected by the gateway. A response of more than about 5.4 MB is not sent inline: the analysis returns about 1.1 KB per line, so this happens from about 5000 lines in one config. Send `Accept: application/large-response.vnd+json` to get a `$payload_ref` URL to the full response instead, or validate fewer lines per request.

MappingCheckContext.description: Where the action sits in its automation or flow

sourceSchema.description: Root of the source entity, `submission` for journeys, the trigger schema otherwise

taskOrder.description: Every action id of the automation in execution order, the ones after the current action included. An action left out is reported as missing (`task-missing`); with validator 0.4.4, an action listed in `taskSchemas` but not here counts as a later one (`task-not-earlier`).

current.description: The action being analysed; must be one of `taskOrder`. Defaults to the last id in `taskOrder`. References to `current` itself or to an action after it are reported as `task-not-earlier`.

producersBySchema.description: Earlier action ids per schema they create, in execution order

path.description: JSON pointer into the config, e.g. `/mapping_attributes/3`; empty for the whole action

valid.description: False when an issue is an error. Only covers the checks that ran: see `skipped_checks`.

skipped_checks.description: Checks that did not run because the request lacks the description they need; `[]` when every check ran. `blocks`: no `roots.source`, so journey blocks and source paths are not checked (`block-removed`, `path-not-in-root`). `attributes`: no `target_root`, so target attributes are not checked (`attribute-not-on-target`). `types`: no `target_root`, so no value is checked against the attribute it fills (`type-mismatch`, `type-converts`, `value-type-mismatch`, `value-not-an-option`). `source-types`: a `target_root` but no `roots.source`, so values copied from the source are not type-checked; fixed values, texts and copies from actions with a `roots.tasks[].description` still are. A description the server loaded (`source`, `config.target_schema`) counts as sent. A `valid: true` with skipped checks does not vouch for those.

reason.description: Why the line has no form, e.g. `op:_each`

why.description: What the rewrite does. `template-syntax`, `nearest-attribute`, `nearest-option` and `operation-key` come with validator 0.4.4. `fallback-producers` (validator 0.6.0): every creator of the schema runs behind a condition, so the line copies from all of them in order. Applying any suggestion adds no error to its line.

context.description: Where the action sits in its automation or flow. Optional: without it the config is checked as the only action of its flow, reading the journey submission (or `source.entity_schema`) and writing `config.target_schema`. Send it only to check references to other actions of the same automation.

target_root.description: Optional description of the target entity's attributes, as built by `rootFromEntitySchema` of `@epilot/entity-mapping-validator`. Each field carries its attribute `type`; with it the validator checks that a source fits the attribute it is mapped to (`type-mismatch`, `type-converts`) and that `_uniq` matches the shared merge keys (`merge-keys-differ`). When left out and `config.target_schema` is set, the server loads that schema.

MappingSourceRef.description: What the automation's trigger provides, by id. Used when `roots.source` is not sent: the server loads the journey's mapping sources (`rootFromMappingSources`) or the entity schema (`rootFromEntitySchema`) with the caller's authorization. A journey or schema that does not exist is an error issue (`source-journey-not-found`, `source-schema-not-found`); one that could not be loaded is a warning (`source-not-loaded`) and the source checks are skipped (`skipped_checks`). Likewise for a target schema (`target-schema-not-found`, `target-schema-not-loaded`). `automation_step` (the trigger of a workflow's automation task) names no data: a warning (`source-not-fixed`) and the source checks are skipped; pass what the workflow was started with instead.

journey_id.description: The triggering journey; its source root is `submission`

entity_schema.description: The slug of the triggering entity's schema, e.g. `contact`

MappingFlowAction.description: An action of an automation (as stored in it), in execution order; only mapping actions are analysed

type.description: `map-entity` and `cart-checkout` are analysed; other actions only count for what they create

config.description: The stored action config (engine JSON); `target_schema` names the schema it writes

actions.description: Every action of the automation in execution order; ids are unique

previous_actions.description: The automation's actions as stored. With them, only issues this change introduced block (`blocking`), matched by action id, target attribute and code.

acknowledged.description: Blocking findings the user decided to keep, after the agent explained them: they stop blocking and are listed in `acknowledged` of the response instead. Send only what the user explicitly accepted. Each matches by action id and code, and by the line's target attribute when `target` is set (without it, every finding of that code in the action). At most 200 entries.

target.description: The target attribute of the line the finding is about

valid.description: True when nothing blocks a save (`blocking` is empty)

blocking.description: What a save gate rejects: per action the errors, the issues on lines whose verdict is `broken` and `value-not-an-option`; with `previous_actions`, only those this change introduced

generated.description: Findings on lines the Journey Builder generated for a journey's default mapping (`origin` `system_recommendation` or `entity_updating_system_recommendation`). The builder regenerates those lines, so these findings are reported but never block.

references.description: Actions that only point at a target of a mapping config (`config.mapping_config`) are checked as that target. `unresolved` lists the actions whose config or target could not be found in the organization; they are left out of the check.

acknowledged.description: Only with `acknowledged` in the request; the blocking findings it matched, which did not block

introduced.description: Only with `previous_actions`; every issue (errors and warnings) this change introduced

analyses.description: The analysis of each mapping action, by action id; other actions have no entry

MappingRoots.description: Optional descriptions of the source and of each action's output (`Roots` of `@epilot/entity-mapping-validator`). A body whose `roots` does not have this shape is rejected with 400.

tasks.description: Every action in execution order; `[]` when there are none

label.description: Display name of what the action creates, e.g. "Contact"

MappingRootDescription.description: What the caller knows about a root (`RootDescription` of `@epilot/entity-mapping-validator`)

open.description: Only partly described; a path below it that `children` does not list is unknown, not missing

truncated.description: the page ceiling was reached; the list is incomplete.

created_by.description: User / service who created the entity mapping config

last_updated_by.description: User / service who last updated entity mapping config

ExecuteRelationsReq.description: Build relations between a source entity and one or more target entities, dynamically identified

source_ref.description: Entity for which to add relations.

main_entity_ref.description: Main Entity from where to locate target entities. Eg. submisssion entity

linkback.description: For cases where you want to store a relation between main entity (eg. submission) and current source entity.

attribute.description: Relation attribute on the main entity (submission) where the target entity will be linked. Set to false to disable linkback

relation_tags.description: Relation tags (labels) to include in main entity linkback relation attribute

outputs.description:
The entities earlier actions (later: Flow tasks) of the same run produced, keyed by the
producing action's id, as on `ExecuteMappingReq.outputs`. `relation_attributes` select them with
`source_filter.output_of`. An output that the main entity's relations also contain is used in
its hydrated form; otherwise its `{ _id, _schema }` reference is enough for the relation write.

source_ref.description: A reference (id and schema) to the entity to be used as source.

loop_ref.description:
Reference to the current iteration's entity when running inside a flow loop.
When set, its fields and relations are merged into the source context;
on schema conflicts the loop entity wins, so paths like `<schema>._id` resolve
to the iteration entity rather than to a same-schema relation of the source.

outputs.description:
The entities earlier steps of the same run produced, keyed by the id of the automation action
(later: Flow task) that produced them, in execution order. The executor passes what it recorded
as each action's `outputs`. A key with an empty list says the action is known to the run but
produced nothing (skipped, failed, or no entity); a mapping that reads it is an ordinary empty
copy. A referenced id with no key at all is reported as an `unresolved_output_reference`
warning, so send every preceding action's id, including the ones that ran nothing.

Mapping attributes read them as `$outputOf['<id>']` (the last entity of that id, so a loop
action yields its latest iteration) and `$outputsOf['<id>']` (every entity of that id);
relation attributes select them with `source_filter.output_of`. An entity is taken from the
source entity's hydrated relations when the producing action linked it back, otherwise it is
fetched by id when a target references the id. Without an entry for an id, the engine falls
back to the relations tagged `_hidden_<id>` (the convention existing configs use).

output_ids.description:
One id per entry in `targets`, in the same order: the id that target's result is published under,
the same key as in `outputs` (the automation action or Flow task that runs the target). Read in preview mode
only: each target's would-be entity becomes the output of its id for the targets after it
(`$outputOf['<id>']`, `source_filter.output_of`), so a chain of actions is previewed as it would
run, instead of reading what an earlier run stored. The response then lists the entities per target
in `preview_targets`.

PreviewTarget.description: What one target would write, in preview mode with `output_ids`

index.description: Position of the target in the request

output_id.description: The id from `output_ids` at this position, which the target's entities were published under

OutputEntityRef.description: One entity an earlier action or task produced

preview_targets.description: In preview mode with `output_ids`, the entities and failure of each target, in order

entity_id.description: id of the source entity to be mapped

Loop_Index_String.description: This string value will be replaced with the value of the loop index, when mapping in loop mode

id.description: Identifier for target configuration. Useful for later usages when trying to identify which target config to map to.

allow_failure.description: Pass it as true, when you don't want failures to interrupt the mapping process.

target_unique.description: Unique key for target entity (see upsertEntity of Entity API)

use_uniqueness_criteria.description: Execution wire flag set per automation by automation-workers: resolve the target entity via the organization's global uniqueness criteria (deduplication-api) instead of target_unique. Never persisted in stored mapping configs.

loop_config.description: contains config in case of running in loop mode

source_path.description: path to the array from the entity payload

source_type.description: Kind of journey block the loop iterates. 'journey-multi-select' (default) is a cards block with multi selection. 'journey-file-upload' is a file upload block: source_path points at the submission's `_files.$relation` array and `filter_tags` narrows it down to the block's files. Forwarded to the flow-level loop by the Automation Hub.

filter_tags.description: Only iterate items of the array whose `_tags` contain every listed tag. Meant for relation arrays such as `submission._files.$relation`, where the journey tags each file relation with the upload block it came from. `##LOOP_INDEX##` keeps referring to the item's index in the unfiltered array.

length.description: a hard limit of how many times the loop is allowed to run.

conditionMode.description: Mode of how conditions are considered valid

conditions.description: Conditions necessary to hold for the target entity to be mapped

linkback_relation_attribute.description: Relation attribute on the main entity where the target entity will be linked. Set to false to disable linkback

linkback_relation_tags.description: Relation tags (labels) to include in main entity linkback relation attribute

graph_context.description:
Multi-hop entity graph lookups resolved before any mapping_attribute is evaluated. Each
entry queries entity-api's `POST /v1/entity:graph` and merges every node's result into
sourceContext under its own `graph.nodes[].id`, so mapping_attributes can `_copy`/`_template`
from `<node id>.<field>`. A graph node's value overwrites any existing sourceContext key of
the same name (a source entity field, a 1-hop relation, or another graph node).

target.description: Target attribute to store the relation in

target_tags.description: Relation tags (labels) to set for the stored relations

target_tags_include_source.description: Include all relation tags (labels) present on the main entity relation

target_entity_tags.description: Tags to add to the matched target entity's _tags array during mapping. Useful for assigning file collections to file entities.

override_with_source_filter.description: Whether to override the relation source_filter with the specified one

source_filter.description: A filter to identify which source entities to pick as relations from main entity

limit.description: Limit relations to maximum number (default, all matched relations)

attribute.description: Filter by a specific relation attribute on the main entity

relation_tag.description: Filter by relation tag (label) on the main entity

output_of.description:
Pick the entities the automation action (later: Flow task) with this id produced in the same run,
as passed in `ExecuteMappingReq.outputs`. Combinable with `schema`, `tag` and `limit`. When the
request carries no entry for the id, the relations tagged `_hidden_<id>` are used instead.

tag.description: Filter by a specific tag on the related entity

self.description: Picks main entity as relation (overrides other filters)

GraphContextEntry.description:
One multi-hop graph lookup against entity-api's `POST /v1/entity:graph`, resolved during
graph_context enrichment (before mapping_attributes are evaluated). Every node in `graph.nodes`
is merged into sourceContext under its own `id`, so listing several nodes here costs one
entity-api call, not one per node.

If a node's `cardinality` is "one" (or it is the seed node), exactly one entity must be found
for it: zero or multiple matches fail the mapping execution instead of silently mapping
missing/wrong data. If "many" (the default), it resolves to an array - possibly empty - with no
such failure. Each node's cardinality is validated independently.

`seed.entity_id` and any `graph.nodes[].filter[].value` may contain `{{handlebars}}` placeholders
(e.g. `{{contract._id}}`, `{{contract.origin_order}}`), resolved against the in-progress
sourceContext (the source entity, its 1-hop relations, and any custom variables already
resolved) before the graph query is sent.

GraphSeed.description: Mirrors entity-api's GraphSeed (see entity-api openapi.yml) - the entity the graph traversal starts from.

entity_id.description: The id of the seed entity. Supports `{{handlebars}}` placeholders resolved against sourceContext.

node_id.description: The node ID in `graph.nodes` that corresponds to the seed entity.

GraphDefinition.description: Mirrors entity-api's GraphDefinition (see entity-api openapi.yml) - the shape of the graph to traverse.

id.description: Unique identifier for this node in the graph definition.

schema.description: Entity schema slug for this node.

cardinality.description:
"one": this node resolves to a single entity. "many" (default if unset): this node
resolves to an array of entities.

fields.description: Optional entity fields to include in the hydrated response for this node.

filter.description:
Narrows this node's traversal results to entities matching every filter (AND semantics).
Useful for disambiguating among multiple entities reachable via the same graph edge.

optional.description:
Only meaningful for a node expected to resolve to a single entity (the seed node, or
"cardinality: one"). When true, finding zero matching entities is not an error - the
mapping proceeds without this node's data instead of failing. Finding more than one
match still fails regardless of this flag; ambiguity is never silently accepted.
On the seed node it also covers an empty seed: when `seed.entity_id` resolves to an
empty value (e.g. an optional source field is missing), the whole graph_context entry
is skipped and none of its nodes are added to the mapping context.

attribute.description: Entity attribute name to match against.

value.description:
Literal value the attribute must exactly equal. Supports `{{handlebars}}` placeholders
resolved against sourceContext when given as a string.

target.description: Target JSON path for the attribute to set

OperationNode.description: Mapping operation nodes are either primitive values or operation node objects

oneOf.description: Unique key consisting of object keys

_copy.description: Copy JSONPath value from source entity context

_template.description: Define handlebars template to output a string

_each.description:
Iterate over a source array. Use with _as and _map.
The value is a path to resolve from the source entity context.
Example: "submission.meterReadings"

_as.description:
Name for the current iteration item in _each.
Accessed as $<name> in _copy paths within _map.
Example: "reading" (accessed as $reading)

_map.description:
Operation to evaluate per _each iteration item.
Can be any OperationNode, typically an object with _copy
references to the $<_as name> alias.

MappingAttributeMode.description: - copy_if_exists - it replaces the target attribute with the source value - append_if_exists - it currently replaces target attribute with array like values. Useful when you have multiple values to be added into one attribute. - set_value - it sets a value to a predefined value. Must be used together with value property.

target.description: JSON like target path for the attribute. Eg. last_name

value.description: Any value to be set: string, number, string[], number[], JSON object, etc. It will override existing values, if any.

target.description: JSON like target path for the attribute. Eg. last_name

source.description: JSON source path for the value to be extracted from the main entity. Eg: steps[1].['Product Info'].price

target.description: JSON like target path for the attribute. Eg. last_name

source.description: JSON source path for the value to be extracted from the main entity. Eg: steps[1].['Product Info'].price

value_json.description: To be provided only when mapping json objects into a target attribute. Eg array of addresses.

target_unique.description: Array of keys which should be used when checking for uniqueness. Eg: [country, city, postal_code]

block_id.description: The journey block's id, the key of its value in `_block_values` of the submission

sub_properties.description: Each item describes a property under the main source and a possibly, a default value for its target attribute

group.description: A group this source belongs to. Used for grouping sources in the UI

possible_target_types.description: Data Structure Type of the underlaying output value

initial_relation.description: Initial value of a relation to be added

title.description: Human readable name of the Source

sub_title.description: Human readable type of the source

repeatable.description: Whether the source (block or attribute) is a repeatable, aka holds a list of values

allowed_ui_actions.description: Describes which actions the user can perform on each target, if specified. If not specified, all actions are allowed

locked.description: Whether its a read-only ui or not. Can be each target, or only the first. Overwrites uiActions

isSingleTarget.description: Whether all source mappings flow into a single attribute (e.g. address)

visibility.description: Determines whether a mapping target should be shown or not. Use if there are targets which cannot be manipulated by the UI. E.g journey_data

possible_target_types.description: Data Structure Type of the underlaying output value

raw.description: Whether the raw value should be used, or whether the value is enriched by a path

param_keys.description: Context parameter keys to look for, as plain strings.

param_ids.description: Accepted and ignored. This service stores context references by name only; the field keeps one request shape across every adapter.

status.description:
partial means the row cap was reached and rows were dropped, or that scanning stopped
early and entire configs - some of which may reference the parameter - were never
scanned.

scanned.description:
The number of configs actually scanned, not the number found. May be less than the
total number of matching configs when status is partial.
